The exterior is off-white with a white interior, but it doesn't feel out of place. The touch of the operating part is recognized better than on a cell phone. I didn't really understand the statement that the remaining time is not visible, but since there is a liquid crystal display on the top of the door, the part is hidden when closed and can be seen as a reflection. However, it's not that frustrating. The dishwasher does its work and the door opens automatically, so time flies while you do your work. 2. Function I tried turning it on in <normal mode> after stirring a pizza cheese dish, mixing coffee, or a spoon left with dairy products on it, and it sparkled as if nothing had happened. The door opens after washing, but I was doing something else and didn't realize how much time had passed, so I almost closed it thinking it was defective. Warm heat and a clean smell leak out. 3. Noise I didn't feel it was loud because it was about the same as the sound of a trombone in a studio apartment. 4. When installing Samsung detergent, they give you an <Ecover discount coupon>, so if you are going to buy Ecover, I recommend waiting a little. I used the Naturepong experience kit, and it was convenient (just put it in without getting powder on your hands. The shell melts on its own) and the cleaning power was good. I will write a comparison review after using the product I bought with the Ecover discount coupon. I have been using the dryer for 4 years, but the dishwasher is an overwhelming innovation. It reduces stress because I can use the dishes without worrying about washing dishes when cooking or drinking tea. Sometimes I have it delivered because of the dishwashing, but I don't think I will order it for that reason. It was really a strange feeling, as if someone had done magic. I recommend it again. 3-month usage review 1. It is more convenient to cut Ecover detergent with scissors than with a knife. 2. The recommended amount is 1/4 of Ecover detergent, but if the dishes are soaked or coffee (latte mix) is pressed into the cup, you should use 1/2 to clean well. 3. When using the Bullim course, the printed part of the custom-made cup may become discolored and the letters may melt. Also, please note that foreign brand cups that can be used in the dishwasher may have fine vertical cracks. 1.

Sentence (English): You need to prepare the space well because it is bigger than you think.
Comments (English): You need to prepare the space well because it is bigger than you think. The technician installed it well at the right time, but if you prepare the water hose hole (white) in advance, you don't need to drill it. The product is much better than not using it while I'm using it. Since it is for 6 people, I have to run it twice a day on cooking days. The bad thing is that you can only add one rinse to the basic course. Maybe three times in total? I hate the lingering detergent smell, so there is no way to add more even if I want to. Please make it so that you can add more like a washing machine during the production stage. Even if you add one cycle and don't use hot air, it takes more than 1:30. Anyway, I bought it because my hands hurt, so I use it well without regret.

For instance, stemmed wine glasses cannot go where they should unless their tray is lowered to prevent obstructing the cutlery drawer. Sentence (English): We've had many other dishwasher brands over the years but this is our first Bosch.
Comments (English): [ Top Notch Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We've had many other dishwasher brands over the years but this is our first Bosch. Without a doubt, this is the quietest unit we've ever had. Pretty amazing. No regrets at all about buying it. I do, though, have a couple points that really cover most any brand of dishwasher. Since they all run so quietly now, would it kill the manufacturers to put some kind of countdown clock on the front? I think another version of the model we got projects a timer onto the floor; ours doesn't have that. Oh well. One minor complaint on our unit: if you want to do a rinse and drain only, it can only be done through an app. There's no button for it on the control panel at all. Through the HomeConnect app, though, you can update the firmware so maybe down the road Bosch will create some kind of button combination that will force it into a rinse/drain mode. Getting the app to recognize our unit took about three times. That was a little frustrating. Other than that, it's a solid dishwasher and not sorry we bought it.

Sentence (English): The product description corresponds to reality.
Comments (English): [ Excellent quality, practical device, good price. ] || ---------------- || The product description corresponds to reality. It provides exactly what is expected. It is no louder (contrary to other people's reviews) than other brands' even higher-priced devices. With the 55-minute "quick" program, it almost surpasses it, but at least it washes the dishes and cutlery at the same level as the previous devices in 130 minutes. The drying performance is impeccable even with this shorter program. It can be used at least 3 times more efficiently during a catering event or a weekend family cookout than its competitors. Quick and efficient help in a household, and it also fit in the place of the previously used (different brand) built-in dishwasher. You don't need an "expert" for installation, you just have to push it into place and the "complicated" installation is complete. Even for an unplanned major maintenance/repair, you won't have to tear down half the kitchen for accessibility. I recommend it with courage and conviction for daily use. The mature technology and decades of manufacturing experience can already be felt on this 2nd series dishwasher.
Comments (Original): [ Kiváló minőség, praktikus készülék, kedvező ár. ] || ---------------- || A termékleírás megfelel a valóságnak. Pont azt nyújtja, ami elvárható. Semmivel sem hangosabb (mások értékeléseivel ellentétben), mint más márka akár magasabb árfekvésű készüléke. Az 55 perces 'gyors' programmal szinte felülmúlja, de legalább olyan szinten mosogatja el az edényeket és evőeszközöket, mint a korábbi készülékek 130 perc alatt. A szárítási teljesítmény kifogástalan még ezzel a rövidebb programmal is. Legalább 3-szor hatékonyabban ki lehet használni egy vendéglátás vagy egy hétvégi családi főzés alkalmával, mint versenytársait. Gyors és hatékony segítség egy háztartásban, ráadásul befért a korábban használt (más márka) beépíthető mosogatógép helyére is. Nem kell 'szakember' a beszereléshez, tényleg csak be kell tolni a helyére és kész a 'bonyolult' telepítés. Még egy nem tervezett nagy karbantartás/javítás miatt sem kell majd lebontani a fél konyhát a hozzáférhetőség miatt. Bátran és meggyőződéssel ajánlom napi használatra. Érezhető a jól kiforrt technológia és a több évtizedes gyártói tapasztalat már ezen a 2. szériás mosogatógépen is.

This is my review of the product. I hope it helps.

Sentence (English): I was going to purchase the 1500$+ one.
Comments (English): [ Excellent dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I was going to purchase the 1500$+ one. After extensive research I settled on this. It's fantastic, cleans dishes perfectly and drys them even better. It also has an extra dry function which is very handy for some things. You can connect it to your phone and adjust the rinseaid quantity, update the dishwasher and download/ add new programs from the app. It notifys your phone when the cycle is completed, when you need to add more rise aid, and tells your when you're running low on tablets. It also tells you when to clean the machine. ( I thought I would never use the app, how stupid a dishwasher has an app right? I was very wrong, it's incredibly handy, especially for looking at energy/water data, programming and adjusting settings) The only difference from the one twice the price is the top shelf isn't height adjustable, completely unnecessary anyway. We throw kids plastic plates/bowls/china/pans and it all comes out very clean and very dry. Don't waste your money on anything more expensive. This dishwasher is absolutely brilliant for the price. It replaced my old bosch, which lasted 10 years.

Sentence (English): After using the dishwasher for about a week, I still have a few programs to try, but I can say that so far the results of the washes are very satisfactory.
Comments (English): [ Happy but needs a quick program. ] || ---------------- || After using the dishwasher for about a week, I still have a few programs to try, but I can say that so far the results of the washes are very satisfactory. The dishwasher has 5 wash programs (Auto, Intensive, Eco, Turbo and Cleaning) and depending on the wash, it has a different water and energy consumption as you can see in one of the attached images. The Turbo program lasts 59 minutes but if you don't use the drying option, which I don't recommend because all the dishes get wet. With the drying option, it increases to 1 hour and 40 minutes. The Eco, although it lasts the longest, to my surprise, is the one that consumes the least water and electricity. You can select the dishwasher load by cleaning only the upper or lower tray, or both. I'm still waiting to try the auto program, which from what I've seen in the instructions, adapts its time and consumption to the dirt detected in the water, so its duration is variable. I have the slight feeling that it has a little more capacity than my previous dishwasher, this may be due to the multitude of positions that both trays have, having space for glasses or for large pans/pots by modifying the position of the rods. We are 4 people living at home and the full load arrives in approximately 3 days, although this is not a relevant fact since it also depends on the optimization of the space that each one makes. The cutlery basket can be put in multiple positions which also optimizes space and the upper tray has two height positions. I can lock the panel so that my little son does not spend all day putting it on since the sound it makes when turning it on and off is very striking (it can be removed). Another thing that can be configured is the water hardness to have optimal washing results. In short, I am happy but I miss a short program.
Comments (Original): [ Contenta pero le falta un programa rápido. ] || ---------------- || Después de estar usando el lavavajillas durante aproximadamente una semana aun me quedan algunos programas por probar pero puedo decir que por ahora los resultados de los lavados son muy satisfactorios. El lavavajillas tiene 5 programas de lavado (Auto, Intensivo, Eco, turbo y limpieza) y dependiendo del lavado que sea Tiene un consumo de agua y energía diferente según podéis ver en una de las imágenes que adjunto. El programa Turbo dura 59 min pero si no se usa la opción de secado, que no recomiendo porque queda toda la vajilla húmeda. Con la opción de secado aumenta a 1 hora y 40 min. El eco aunque es el que más dura, para mi sorpresa es el que menos consume tanto agua como electricidad. Se puede seleccionar la carga de lavavajillas haciendo solo limpieza de bandeja superior, inferior o ambas. Tengo pendiente a probar el programa auto, que por lo que he visto en las instrucciones, adapta su tiempo y consumo a la suciedad que se detecte en el agua por lo que su duración es variable. Tengo la ligera sensación de que tiene un poco mas de capacidad que mi anterior lavavajillas, esto puede ser debido a la multitud de posición de la que disponen ambas bandejas teniendo espacio para las copas o para sartenes/ollas de gran volumen modificando la posición de las varillas. En casa somos 4 personas viviendo y llego la carga completa en aproximadamente 3 días, aunque esto no es un dato relevante ya que también depende de la optimización del espacio que haga cada uno. La cesta de los cubiertos se puede poner en múltiples posiciones lo que optimiza también el espacio y la bandeja superior tiene dos posiciones en altura. Puedo bloquear el panel para que mi hijo pequeño no ande todo el día poniéndolo en funcionamiento ya que el sonido que emite al encender y apagar es muy llamativo (se puede quitar). Otra cosa que se puede configurar es la dureza del agua para tener así resultados óptimos de lavado. En resumidas cuentas, estoy contenta pero echo de menos un programa corto

Installation was not so great. ] || ---------------- || We loved our last Bosch dishwasher and it outlasted and outperformed all of our other appliances so we decided to replace it with another Bosch. Costco had a decent price especially since it came with installation. Now, I had heard from others that installation didn't always happen for people in certain parts of the state so I called Costco to verify. I called more than once because I didn't want the dishwasher to sit around while I scheduled an installer. Every time I asked, I was assured that the product came with installation in my location. "You are getting white glove service," I was told. However, when the product was dropped off, the delivery people said that Costco would be calling me in 15 minutes to conform the installation. Fifteen minutes turned into an hour and then 90 minutes so I called Costco only to be told that, "No, this product does not come with installation in your area." So. I had to arrange for my own installation after all. Most appliances aren't a problem, but this one was hard-wired into our electrical system so it was a bit trickier. Needless to say, I was not happy, especially since I got confirmation of installation multiple times. There is a serious disconnect between Costco and the delivery/installation teams they work with. Now, the dishwasher is amazing. We love it. I am still pretty annoyed about the installation experience though.

Comments (English): [ No Installation Instructions Provided ] || ---------------- || This is a nice dishwasher, but there were a handful of issues which caused us problems. I thought we were just getting a simple, plug-n-play 24" standard dishwasher, but everything seems more complicated than it was 15 years ago.First, at the time we ordered it, we thought that we were ordering a microwave with a stainless steel interior ( like the Bosch we had previously ), but it came with a grey plastic interior, so we should have paid more attention to the description rather than the pictures.Second, when we were ready to install it, we discovered that there were no installation instructions. There were quick guide sheets, a plastic label we could attach to the top panel to get better results rinsing, a user's manual ( in 3 languages ) and a product guide, but no installation manual. We had to go back to Lowe's and get assistance downloading the manual from a clerk in the Appliances section. This held us up. Third, it didn't come with a cord. Apparently, this is common nowadays, but they used to be standard. Fortunately, we had a spare in the shop. We also had to get a hose connector with a right-angle hookup reducer to attach to the water feed.Once we got everything installed, it worked fine and we got a good value for it. I just don't like 'gotchas'. This felt like just another way to get additional money out of consumers.Hope this helps someone shopping for dishwashers.

Sentence (English): I am leaving a review of my purchase process and first dishwasher in case it will be helpful to those who are having trouble buying their first dishwasher like me.
Comments (English): I am leaving a review of my purchase process and first dishwasher in case it will be helpful to those who are having trouble buying their first dishwasher like me. First of all, I am a father and a man. Like many housewives, I had no information or experience, so I searched for products and reviews for almost a month. The more I searched, the more confused I became and the more difficult it was to decide;;; I narrowed down the candidates by setting criteria. 1. Mid-low priced model so I might regret buying it. 2. Less than 10% of all reviews had 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (interior stainless steel) 4. After-sales service period 5. Size that does not take up much space on the sink. 1) It seemed to be verified to be in the 200,000 to 300,000 won range. 2-3) People with dishwasher experience are able to clearly distinguish the pros and cons of a used product and a new one, so the ratings are generally low. (Interior walls are stainless steel. Bottom is not stainless steel) 4) 2-year warranty from Coupang. 5) The single-tier model takes up a lot of space as the bottom area for storing dishes is wide, so I chose the 2-tier basket model. (When the door is opened) (I pulled a tape measure on the sink to see the size) Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Reinstalled on Monday -> Washed the dishes in the evening with the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe in case I was changing the door direction, but it was shorter than I thought, so the installer kindly did it one more time and changed the direction) Commute, come home from work, have dinner, wash dishes, do laundry, do housework, then go to bed, then go to work again;;; It's a repetition. This dishwasher is so convenient - My first day with the dishwasher. I made curry rice with meat for dinner tonight, and I'm worried about the cleaning power, but I want to test it in an extremely strong environment for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice starch from the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, utensils, and kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature and it took 80 minutes. (The time decreased) The dishes were done after 12 minutes, but it started to cool down after that. After 3 minutes, the door opened and steam came up. Out of curiosity, I lifted my hand on the back of the top and it was hot. - After about 5 minutes? I took it out and the color was different. How did it feel when I washed the kids for the first time in a while? Clothes that were washed in a washing machine at 30 degrees Celsius but occasionally washed at 60 degrees Celsius or higher? That kind of feeling? - The stuff that gets stuck slightly when cooking on the inside of the stainless steel pot can't be washed. Since it's soaked, I can easily clean it by rubbing it in cold water as if I was washing dishes. # I took out the 2-tier basket to put a large pot and cutting board in, but this seems more convenient. # The detergent is marked as 7 grams, but I didn't know and bought 10 grams so I did it without any problems (7 grams doesn't seem to be common) # I didn't want to drill a hole, so I took out an unused detergent container attached to the sink in advance and asked them to put the pipe in there, and it fits perfectly. # The only noise I can't tell is the sound of it draining two or three times. First of all, I am a father and a man. Like many housewives, I had no information or experience, so I searched for products and reviews for almost a month. The more I searched, the more confused I became and the more difficult it was to decide;;; I narrowed down the candidates by setting criteria. 1. Mid-low priced model so I might regret buying it. 2. Less than 10% of all reviews had 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (interior stainless steel) 4. After-sales service period 5. Size that does not take up much space on the sink. 1) It seemed to be verified to be in the 200,000 to 300,000 won range. 2-3) People with dishwasher experience are able to clearly distinguish the pros and cons of a used product and a new one, so the ratings are generally low. (Interior walls are stainless steel. Bottom is not stainless steel) 4) 2-year warranty from Coupang. 5) The single-tier model takes up a lot of space as the bottom area for storing dishes is wide, so I chose the 2-tier basket model. (When the door is opened) (I pulled a tape measure on the sink to see the size) Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Reinstalled on Monday -> Washed the dishes in the evening with the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe in case I was changing the door direction, but it was shorter than I thought, so the installer kindly did it one more time and changed the direction) Commute, come home from work, have dinner, wash dishes, do laundry, do housework, then go to bed, then go to work again;;; It's a repetition. This dishwasher is so convenient - My first day with the dishwasher. I made curry rice with meat for dinner tonight, and I'm worried about the cleaning power, but I want to test it in an extremely strong environment for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice starch from the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, utensils, and kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature and it took 80 minutes. (The time decreased) The dishes were done after 12 minutes, but it started to cool down after that. After 3 minutes, the door opened and steam came up. Out of curiosity, I lifted my hand on the back of the top and it was hot. - After about 5 minutes? I took it out and the color was different. How did it feel when I washed the kids for the first time in a while? Clothes that were washed in a washing machine at 30 degrees Celsius but occasionally washed at 60 degrees Celsius or higher? That kind of feeling? - The stuff that gets stuck slightly when cooking on the inside of the stainless steel pot can't be washed. Since it's soaked, I can easily clean it by rubbing it in cold water as if I was washing dishes. # I took out the 2-tier basket to put a large pot and cutting board in, but this seems more convenient. # The detergent is marked as 7 grams, but I didn't know and bought 10 grams so I did it without any problems (7 grams doesn't seem to be common) # I didn't want to drill a hole, so I took out an unused detergent container attached to the sink in advance and asked them to put the pipe in there, and it fits perfectly. # The only noise I can't tell is the sound of it draining two or three times. In my opinion. For those new to dishwashing, no matter which brand you choose, you'll definitely experience a new world of convenience and comfort. I'm thinking about exercising in the evenings. Let's just do it and live comfortably.

Out of curiosity, I lifted my hand on the back of the top and it was hot. - After about 5 minutes? I took it out and the color was different. How did it feel when I washed the kids for the first time in a while? Clothes that were washed in a washing machine at 30 degrees Celsius but occasionally washed at 60 degrees Celsius or higher? The more I searched, the more confused I became and the more difficult it was to decide;;; I narrowed down the candidates by setting criteria. 1. Mid-low priced model so I might regret buying it. 2. Size that does not take up much space on the sink. 1) It seemed to be verified to be in the 200,000 to 300,000 won range. 2-3) People with dishwasher experience are able to clearly distinguish the pros and cons of a used product and a new one, so the ratings are generally low. (Interior walls are stainless steel. Bottom is not stainless steel) 4) 2-year warranty from Coupang. 5) The single-tier model takes up a lot of space as the bottom area for storing dishes is wide, so I chose the 2-tier basket model. (When the door is opened) (I pulled a tape measure on the sink to see the size) Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Reinstalled on Monday -> Washed the dishes in the evening with the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe in case I was changing the door direction, but it was shorter than I thought, so the installer kindly did it one more time and changed the direction) Commute, come home from work, have dinner, wash dishes, do laundry, do housework, then go to bed, then go to work again;;; It's a repetition. This dishwasher is so convenient - My first day with the dishwasher. I made curry rice with meat for dinner tonight, and I'm worried about the cleaning power, but I want to test it in an extremely strong environment for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice starch from the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, utensils, and kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature and it took 80 minutes. Out of curiosity, I lifted my hand on the back of the top and it was hot. - After about 5 minutes? I took it out and the color was different. How did it feel when I washed the kids for the first time in a while? Clothes that were washed in a washing machine at 30 degrees Celsius but occasionally washed at 60 degrees Celsius or higher? That kind of feeling? - The stuff that gets stuck slightly when cooking on the inside of the stainless steel pot can't be washed. Since it's soaked, I can easily clean it by rubbing it in cold water as if I was washing dishes. # I took out the 2-tier basket to put a large pot and cutting board in, but this seems more convenient. # The detergent is marked as 7 grams, but I didn't know and bought 10 grams so I did it without any problems (7 grams doesn't seem to be common) # I didn't want to drill a hole, so I took out an unused detergent container attached to the sink in advance and asked them to put the pipe in there, and it fits perfectly. # The only noise I can't tell is the sound of it draining two or three times. Let's just do it and live comfortably.

Less than 10% of all reviews had 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (interior stainless steel) 4. After-sales service period 5. Size that does not take up much space on the sink. 1) It seemed to be verified to be in the 200,000 to 300,000 won range. 2-3) People with dishwasher experience are able to clearly distinguish the pros and cons of a used product and a new one, so the ratings are generally low. (Interior walls are stainless steel. Bottom is not stainless steel) 4) 2-year warranty from Coupang. 5) The single-tier model takes up a lot of space as the bottom area for storing dishes is wide, so I chose the 2-tier basket model. (When the door is opened) (I pulled a tape measure on the sink to see the size) Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Reinstalled on Monday -> Washed the dishes in the evening with the dishwasher. This dishwasher is so convenient - My first day with the dishwasher. I made curry rice with meat for dinner tonight, and I'm worried about the cleaning power, but I want to test it in an extremely strong environment for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice starch from the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, utensils, and kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature and it took 80 minutes. (The time decreased) The dishes were done after 12 minutes, but it started to cool down after that. After 3 minutes, the door opened and steam came up. Out of curiosity, I lifted my hand on the back of the top and it was hot. - After about 5 minutes? I took it out and the color was different. How did it feel when I washed the kids for the first time in a while? Clothes that were washed in a washing machine at 30 degrees Celsius but occasionally washed at 60 degrees Celsius or higher? That kind of feeling? - The stuff that gets stuck slightly when cooking on the inside of the stainless steel pot can't be washed. Comments (English): I am leaving a review of my purchase process and first dishwasher in case it will be helpful to those who are having trouble buying their first dishwasher like me. First of all, I am a father and a man. Like many housewives, I had no information or experience, so I searched for products and reviews for almost a month. The more I searched, the more confused I became and the more difficult it was to decide;;; I narrowed down the candidates by setting criteria. 1. Mid-low priced model so I might regret buying it. 2. Less than 10% of all reviews had 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (interior stainless steel) 4. After-sales service period 5. Size that does not take up much space on the sink. 1) It seemed to be verified to be in the 200,000 to 300,000 won range. 2-3) People with dishwasher experience are able to clearly distinguish the pros and cons of a used product and a new one, so the ratings are generally low. (Interior walls are stainless steel. Bottom is not stainless steel) 4) 2-year warranty from Coupang. 5) The single-tier model takes up a lot of space as the bottom area for storing dishes is wide, so I chose the 2-tier basket model. (When the door is opened) (I pulled a tape measure on the sink to see the size) Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Reinstalled on Monday -> Washed the dishes in the evening with the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe in case I was changing the door direction, but it was shorter than I thought, so the installer kindly did it one more time and changed the direction) Commute, come home from work, have dinner, wash dishes, do laundry, do housework, then go to bed, then go to work again;;; It's a repetition. This dishwasher is so convenient - My first day with the dishwasher. I made curry rice with meat for dinner tonight, and I'm worried about the cleaning power, but I want to test it in an extremely strong environment for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice starch from the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, utensils, and kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature and it took 80 minutes. (The time decreased) The dishes were done after 12 minutes, but it started to cool down after that. After 3 minutes, the door opened and steam came up. Out of curiosity, I lifted my hand on the back of the top and it was hot. - After about 5 minutes? I took it out and the color was different. How did it feel when I washed the kids for the first time in a while? Clothes that were washed in a washing machine at 30 degrees Celsius but occasionally washed at 60 degrees Celsius or higher? That kind of feeling? - The stuff that gets stuck slightly when cooking on the inside of the stainless steel pot can't be washed. Since it's soaked, I can easily clean it by rubbing it in cold water as if I was washing dishes. # I took out the 2-tier basket to put a large pot and cutting board in, but this seems more convenient. # The detergent is marked as 7 grams, but I didn't know and bought 10 grams so I did it without any problems (7 grams doesn't seem to be common) # I didn't want to drill a hole, so I took out an unused detergent container attached to the sink in advance and asked them to put the pipe in there, and it fits perfectly. # The only noise I can't tell is the sound of it draining two or three times. Comments (English): I am leaving a review of my purchase process and first dishwasher in case it will be helpful to those who are having trouble buying their first dishwasher like me. First of all, I am a father and a man. Like many housewives, I had no information or experience, so I searched for products and reviews for almost a month. The more I searched, the more confused I became and the more difficult it was to decide;;; I narrowed down the candidates by setting criteria. 1. Mid-low priced model so I might regret buying it. 2. Less than 10% of all reviews had 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (interior stainless steel) 4. After-sales service period 5. Size that does not take up much space on the sink. 1) It seemed to be verified to be in the 200,000 to 300,000 won range. 2-3) People with dishwasher experience are able to clearly distinguish the pros and cons of a used product and a new one, so the ratings are generally low. (Interior walls are stainless steel. Bottom is not stainless steel) 4) 2-year warranty from Coupang. 5) The single-tier model takes up a lot of space as the bottom area for storing dishes is wide, so I chose the 2-tier basket model. (When the door is opened) (I pulled a tape measure on the sink to see the size) Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Reinstalled on Monday -> Washed the dishes in the evening with the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe in case I was changing the door direction, but it was shorter than I thought, so the installer kindly did it one more time and changed the direction) Commute, come home from work, have dinner, wash dishes, do laundry, do housework, then go to bed, then go to work again;;; It's a repetition. This dishwasher is so convenient - My first day with the dishwasher. I made curry rice with meat for dinner tonight, and I'm worried about the cleaning power, but I want to test it in an extremely strong environment for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice starch from the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, utensils, and kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature and it took 80 minutes. (The time decreased) The dishes were done after 12 minutes, but it started to cool down after that. After 3 minutes, the door opened and steam came up. Out of curiosity, I lifted my hand on the back of the top and it was hot. - After about 5 minutes? I took it out and the color was different. How did it feel when I washed the kids for the first time in a while? Clothes that were washed in a washing machine at 30 degrees Celsius but occasionally washed at 60 degrees Celsius or higher? Size that does not take up much space on the sink. 1) It seemed to be verified to be in the 200,000 to 300,000 won range. 2-3) People with dishwasher experience are able to clearly distinguish the pros and cons of a used product and a new one, so the ratings are generally low. Sentence (English): My old dishwasher broke down, so I needed a new one.
Comments (English): [ Top-notch dishwasher with excellent results ] || ---------------- || My old dishwasher broke down, so I needed a new one. Naturally, I wanted to keep up with the latest technology, so only a smart dishwasher was an option. We also had the option of an extra-large model, since our kitchen countertop is high enough to accommodate a dishwasher that's 5 cm taller. The dishwasher has interior lighting, which I find very helpful. It also has a digital display that projects important information onto the floor, intelligent programs that adapt to individual needs, and smart connectivity, allowing me to program and start the dishwasher remotely. So far, I have absolutely no complaints.
Comments (Original): [ 1A Geschirrspüler mit hervorragenden Ergebnissen ] || ---------------- || Mein alter Geschirrspüler war defekt, daher musste ein neuer her. Man möchte natürlich mit dem aktuellen Stand der Technik mitgehen, daher kam nur ein smartes Gerät in Frage. Dann hatten wir nun auch die Option ein XXL Gerät zu verwenden, da unsere Arbeitsplatte in der Küche hoch genug verbaut ist und daher ausreichend Platz für ein 5cm höheres Gerät bietet. Das Gerät hat nun Innenbeleuchtung, was ich sehr hilfreich finde. Eine digitale Anzeige, die wichtige Infos auf den Boden projeziert. Intelligente Programme, die sich nach individuellen Bedürfnissen ausrichten und eine smarte Anbindung, sodass man die Spülmaschine von der Ferne aus programmieren und starten kann. Bisher kann ich über absolut nichts meckern.

Sentence (English): I am sharing my purchasing process and my first dishwasher review in case it helps those who, like me, are struggling with their first purchase.
Comments (English): I am sharing my purchasing process and my first dishwasher review in case it helps those who, like me, are struggling with their first purchase. First off, I am a dad. Since I lacked the information and experience that moms and housewives might, I spent nearly a month searching for products and reviews. The more I searched, the more confused I became, and the harder it was to make a decision. I set criteria to narrow down my candidates: 1. Mid-range models in case I regretted buying them later. 2. Less than 10% of total reviews must have 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (stainless steel interior). 4. Warranty period. 5. Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. (Interior walls are stainless steel, but the bottom is not). 4) Coupang offers a 2-year warranty. 5) I chose the 2-tier basket type because the 1-tier model takes up too much space due to the large surface area for dishes. (I even measured the size with a tape measure pulled from the sink with the door open). Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Re-installed on Monday ->. I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe length in case I needed to change the door direction, but it was shorter than expected, so the installer kindly adjusted it again and changed the direction.) It's a cycle of going to work, coming home, dinner, washing dishes, doing laundry, doing housework, then sleeping, and then going to work again... Ah. This dishwasher is so convenient. - First day with the dishwasher. I cooked curry rice with meat for dinner tonight. I was worried about the cleaning power, but I wanted to test it out in extreme conditions for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice grains at the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, dishes, cutlery, and the kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature, so it took 80 minutes. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Or like fresh clothes after occasionally washing them at 60 degrees or higher in a washing machine that usually runs at 30 degrees? That kind of feeling. - The slightly burnt-on residue inside the stainless steel pot from cooking didn't come off. Since it was soaked, I scrubbed it in cold water just like hand-washing, and it cleaned up easily. # I removed the 2-tier basket to put large pots and cutting boards in, and I think this is more convenient. # The detergent is marked for 7 grams, but I unknowingly bought 10 grams, so I just used that and there were no problems (7-gram bottles seem to be hard to find). I didn't want to drill a hole, so I removed an unused detergent container from the sink beforehand and asked them to run the pipes through there, and it fits perfectly. As for noise, I don't notice anything other than the sound of the water draining two or three times. For those new to dishwashers, no matter which brand you choose, it will definitely be more convenient than not having one, and I think you will experience a whole new world. I think I'll try working out this evening. Let's just go for it and live comfortably~~~~~
Comments (Original): 저처럼 식세기 첫구매 고민 많이하는분들 도움 되려나해서 구매과정 과 첫식세기 후기 남겨봅니다.우선 저는 아빠남자 입니다.엄마주부들 처럼 정보도 경험도 없어서 거의 한달동안 제품, 후기 검색 했습니다.검색할수록 혼란스럽고 결정 더못하겠더라구요;;;저는 기준을 세워서 후보군을 추렸습니다.1.사놓고 후회할지 모르니 중저가형.2.전체후기 중 별1~3개가 10%이하.3.세척력+내구성(내부스텐)4.AS기간5.싱크대위 공간을 많이 차지하지 않는 크기.1)20~30만원대가 검증된 것으로 보였음.2~3)식세기 경험있는 분들은 써왔던 제품과 새 제품의 장단점이 명확히 구분할수 있는 능력자 이므로 대체로 별점이 낮은편으로 분석 됨.(내부 벽은 스텐. 바닥은 스텐아님)4)쿠팡에서 2년 보장.5)1단은 식기넣는 바닥면적이 넓은만큼 공간을 많이 차지해서 바스켓2단 형으로 선택.(문열렸을때 사이즈까지 싱크대에서 줄자 당겨봄)》토요일구매->일요일설치->월요일재설치->저녁 설거지를 식세기로 함.(문방향 바꿀거 대비 배관길게 요청했는데 생각보다 짧게되있어서 설치기사님이 친절하게 한번더해주시고 방향바꿈)출근,퇴근,저녁식사,설겆이빨래집안일 하면 취침, 또출근;;; 반복인데아..식세기 이거 너무 편해요- 식세기 첫날. 오늘저녁 고기넣은카레라이스 해먹고세척력걱정은되고, 극강의환경에서 첫테스트는 해보고싶고.- 싱크대수도에서 밥풀만대충떼고 기름기많은 냄비,도마,그릇수저,애들물병 다 넣음.- 고온설정 하니까 80분. (시간은줄어듬)12분됐을때 설거지는 완료되나 그때부터 열식힘. 3분되니 문열리고 스팀쫙 올라옴. 호기심에 윗판뒷판 손올려보니 뒷판은 뜨끈뜨큰함.- 5분?정도 더 지나고 꺼내보니 땟깔부터 다름.애들 간만에 때밀었을때 전후 느낌? 30도물에 세탁기돌리다가 가끔씩60도 또는 그이상온도로 세탁후 깨운한 옷? 그런느낌?ㅋ- 스텐냄비 안쪽 조리할때 살짝눌러붙은건 세척안됨. 불려진상태라 찬물에 손설겆이하듯이 문지르니 쉽게 깨끗해짐.# 큰냄비,도마 넣으려고 2층바스켓 뺏는데 이게 더편한것 같아요.# 세제는 7그람표시 되있는데, 모르고 10g 사놔서 그냥했지만 아무문제 없어요(7그람은 잘없는듯)# 타공 안하고싶어서 미리 싱크대에 달려있는 안쓰는 세제통빼내놓고, 거기로 배관넣어 달라고 했는데 찰떡이네요.#소음은 두세번 배수될때 소리말곤 모르겠어요.☆제 생각엔.. 식세기 처음인 분들은 어떤브랜드를 선택해도 없을때보단 무조건 편하고 신세계를 경험할것 같아요.이제 저녁에 운동 해볼까 합니다.일단 저지르고 편하게 삽시다~~~~~

Sentence (English): Since I lacked the information and experience that moms and housewives might, I spent nearly a month searching for products and reviews.
Comments (English): I am sharing my purchasing process and my first dishwasher review in case it helps those who, like me, are struggling with their first purchase. First off, I am a dad. Since I lacked the information and experience that moms and housewives might, I spent nearly a month searching for products and reviews. The more I searched, the more confused I became, and the harder it was to make a decision. I set criteria to narrow down my candidates: 1. Mid-range models in case I regretted buying them later. 2. Less than 10% of total reviews must have 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (stainless steel interior). 4. Warranty period. 5. Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. (Interior walls are stainless steel, but the bottom is not). 4) Coupang offers a 2-year warranty. 5) I chose the 2-tier basket type because the 1-tier model takes up too much space due to the large surface area for dishes. (I even measured the size with a tape measure pulled from the sink with the door open). Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Re-installed on Monday ->. I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe length in case I needed to change the door direction, but it was shorter than expected, so the installer kindly adjusted it again and changed the direction.) It's a cycle of going to work, coming home, dinner, washing dishes, doing laundry, doing housework, then sleeping, and then going to work again... Ah. This dishwasher is so convenient. - First day with the dishwasher. I cooked curry rice with meat for dinner tonight. I was worried about the cleaning power, but I wanted to test it out in extreme conditions for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice grains at the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, dishes, cutlery, and the kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature, so it took 80 minutes. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Or like fresh clothes after occasionally washing them at 60 degrees or higher in a washing machine that usually runs at 30 degrees? That kind of feeling. - The slightly burnt-on residue inside the stainless steel pot from cooking didn't come off. Since it was soaked, I scrubbed it in cold water just like hand-washing, and it cleaned up easily. # I removed the 2-tier basket to put large pots and cutting boards in, and I think this is more convenient. # The detergent is marked for 7 grams, but I unknowingly bought 10 grams, so I just used that and there were no problems (7-gram bottles seem to be hard to find). I didn't want to drill a hole, so I removed an unused detergent container from the sink beforehand and asked them to run the pipes through there, and it fits perfectly. As for noise, I don't notice anything other than the sound of the water draining two or three times. For those new to dishwashers, no matter which brand you choose, it will definitely be more convenient than not having one, and I think you will experience a whole new world. I think I'll try working out this evening. Let's just go for it and live comfortably~~~~~

Sentence (English): Less than 10% of total reviews must have 1 to 3 stars.
Comments (English): I am sharing my purchasing process and my first dishwasher review in case it helps those who, like me, are struggling with their first purchase. First off, I am a dad. Since I lacked the information and experience that moms and housewives might, I spent nearly a month searching for products and reviews. The more I searched, the more confused I became, and the harder it was to make a decision. I set criteria to narrow down my candidates: 1. Mid-range models in case I regretted buying them later. 2. Less than 10% of total reviews must have 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (stainless steel interior). 4. Warranty period. 5. Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. (Interior walls are stainless steel, but the bottom is not). 4) Coupang offers a 2-year warranty. 5) I chose the 2-tier basket type because the 1-tier model takes up too much space due to the large surface area for dishes. (I even measured the size with a tape measure pulled from the sink with the door open). Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Re-installed on Monday ->. I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe length in case I needed to change the door direction, but it was shorter than expected, so the installer kindly adjusted it again and changed the direction.) It's a cycle of going to work, coming home, dinner, washing dishes, doing laundry, doing housework, then sleeping, and then going to work again... Ah. This dishwasher is so convenient. - First day with the dishwasher. I cooked curry rice with meat for dinner tonight. I was worried about the cleaning power, but I wanted to test it out in extreme conditions for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice grains at the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, dishes, cutlery, and the kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature, so it took 80 minutes. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Or like fresh clothes after occasionally washing them at 60 degrees or higher in a washing machine that usually runs at 30 degrees? That kind of feeling. - The slightly burnt-on residue inside the stainless steel pot from cooking didn't come off. Since it was soaked, I scrubbed it in cold water just like hand-washing, and it cleaned up easily. # I removed the 2-tier basket to put large pots and cutting boards in, and I think this is more convenient. # The detergent is marked for 7 grams, but I unknowingly bought 10 grams, so I just used that and there were no problems (7-gram bottles seem to be hard to find). I didn't want to drill a hole, so I removed an unused detergent container from the sink beforehand and asked them to run the pipes through there, and it fits perfectly. As for noise, I don't notice anything other than the sound of the water draining two or three times. For those new to dishwashers, no matter which brand you choose, it will definitely be more convenient than not having one, and I think you will experience a whole new world. I think I'll try working out this evening. Let's just go for it and live comfortably~~~~~

Comments (English): I am sharing my purchasing process and my first dishwasher review in case it helps those who, like me, are struggling with their first purchase. First off, I am a dad. Since I lacked the information and experience that moms and housewives might, I spent nearly a month searching for products and reviews. The more I searched, the more confused I became, and the harder it was to make a decision. I set criteria to narrow down my candidates: 1. Mid-range models in case I regretted buying them later. 2. Less than 10% of total reviews must have 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (stainless steel interior). 4. Warranty period. 5. Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. (Interior walls are stainless steel, but the bottom is not). 4) Coupang offers a 2-year warranty. 5) I chose the 2-tier basket type because the 1-tier model takes up too much space due to the large surface area for dishes. (I even measured the size with a tape measure pulled from the sink with the door open). Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Re-installed on Monday ->. I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe length in case I needed to change the door direction, but it was shorter than expected, so the installer kindly adjusted it again and changed the direction.) It's a cycle of going to work, coming home, dinner, washing dishes, doing laundry, doing housework, then sleeping, and then going to work again... Ah. This dishwasher is so convenient. - First day with the dishwasher. I cooked curry rice with meat for dinner tonight. I was worried about the cleaning power, but I wanted to test it out in extreme conditions for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice grains at the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, dishes, cutlery, and the kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature, so it took 80 minutes. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Or like fresh clothes after occasionally washing them at 60 degrees or higher in a washing machine that usually runs at 30 degrees? That kind of feeling. - The slightly burnt-on residue inside the stainless steel pot from cooking didn't come off. Since it was soaked, I scrubbed it in cold water just like hand-washing, and it cleaned up easily. # I removed the 2-tier basket to put large pots and cutting boards in, and I think this is more convenient. # The detergent is marked for 7 grams, but I unknowingly bought 10 grams, so I just used that and there were no problems (7-gram bottles seem to be hard to find). I didn't want to drill a hole, so I removed an unused detergent container from the sink beforehand and asked them to run the pipes through there, and it fits perfectly. As for noise, I don't notice anything other than the sound of the water draining two or three times. For those new to dishwashers, no matter which brand you choose, it will definitely be more convenient than not having one, and I think you will experience a whole new world. I think I'll try working out this evening. Let's just go for it and live comfortably~~~~~

Comments (English): I am sharing my purchasing process and my first dishwasher review in case it helps those who, like me, are struggling with their first purchase. First off, I am a dad. Since I lacked the information and experience that moms and housewives might, I spent nearly a month searching for products and reviews. The more I searched, the more confused I became, and the harder it was to make a decision. I set criteria to narrow down my candidates: 1. Mid-range models in case I regretted buying them later. 2. Less than 10% of total reviews must have 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (stainless steel interior). 4. Warranty period. 5. Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. (Interior walls are stainless steel, but the bottom is not). 4) Coupang offers a 2-year warranty. 5) I chose the 2-tier basket type because the 1-tier model takes up too much space due to the large surface area for dishes. (I even measured the size with a tape measure pulled from the sink with the door open). Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Re-installed on Monday ->. I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe length in case I needed to change the door direction, but it was shorter than expected, so the installer kindly adjusted it again and changed the direction.) It's a cycle of going to work, coming home, dinner, washing dishes, doing laundry, doing housework, then sleeping, and then going to work again... Ah. This dishwasher is so convenient. - First day with the dishwasher. I cooked curry rice with meat for dinner tonight. I was worried about the cleaning power, but I wanted to test it out in extreme conditions for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice grains at the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, dishes, cutlery, and the kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature, so it took 80 minutes. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Or like fresh clothes after occasionally washing them at 60 degrees or higher in a washing machine that usually runs at 30 degrees? That kind of feeling. - The slightly burnt-on residue inside the stainless steel pot from cooking didn't come off. Since it was soaked, I scrubbed it in cold water just like hand-washing, and it cleaned up easily. # I removed the 2-tier basket to put large pots and cutting boards in, and I think this is more convenient. # The detergent is marked for 7 grams, but I unknowingly bought 10 grams, so I just used that and there were no problems (7-gram bottles seem to be hard to find). I didn't want to drill a hole, so I removed an unused detergent container from the sink beforehand and asked them to run the pipes through there, and it fits perfectly. As for noise, I don't notice anything other than the sound of the water draining two or three times. For those new to dishwashers, no matter which brand you choose, it will definitely be more convenient than not having one, and I think you will experience a whole new world. I think I'll try working out this evening. Let's just go for it and live comfortably~~~~~

The more I searched, the more confused I became, and the harder it was to make a decision. I set criteria to narrow down my candidates: 1. Mid-range models in case I regretted buying them later. 2. Less than 10% of total reviews must have 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (stainless steel interior). 4. Warranty period. 5. Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. (Interior walls are stainless steel, but the bottom is not). 4) Coupang offers a 2-year warranty. 5) I chose the 2-tier basket type because the 1-tier model takes up too much space due to the large surface area for dishes. (I even measured the size with a tape measure pulled from the sink with the door open). Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Re-installed on Monday ->. I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe length in case I needed to change the door direction, but it was shorter than expected, so the installer kindly adjusted it again and changed the direction.) It's a cycle of going to work, coming home, dinner, washing dishes, doing laundry, doing housework, then sleeping, and then going to work again... Ah. This dishwasher is so convenient. - First day with the dishwasher. I cooked curry rice with meat for dinner tonight. I was worried about the cleaning power, but I wanted to test it out in extreme conditions for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice grains at the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, dishes, cutlery, and the kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature, so it took 80 minutes. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Or like fresh clothes after occasionally washing them at 60 degrees or higher in a washing machine that usually runs at 30 degrees? That kind of feeling. - The slightly burnt-on residue inside the stainless steel pot from cooking didn't come off. Since it was soaked, I scrubbed it in cold water just like hand-washing, and it cleaned up easily. # I removed the 2-tier basket to put large pots and cutting boards in, and I think this is more convenient. # The detergent is marked for 7 grams, but I unknowingly bought 10 grams, so I just used that and there were no problems (7-gram bottles seem to be hard to find). I didn't want to drill a hole, so I removed an unused detergent container from the sink beforehand and asked them to run the pipes through there, and it fits perfectly. As for noise, I don't notice anything other than the sound of the water draining two or three times. For those new to dishwashers, no matter which brand you choose, it will definitely be more convenient than not having one, and I think you will experience a whole new world. I think I'll try working out this evening. Let's just go for it and live comfortably~~~~~

Sentence (English): I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (
Comments (English): I am sharing my purchasing process and my first dishwasher review in case it helps those who, like me, are struggling with their first purchase. First off, I am a dad. Since I lacked the information and experience that moms and housewives might, I spent nearly a month searching for products and reviews. The more I searched, the more confused I became, and the harder it was to make a decision. I set criteria to narrow down my candidates: 1. Mid-range models in case I regretted buying them later. 2. Less than 10% of total reviews must have 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (stainless steel interior). 4. Warranty period. 5. Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. (Interior walls are stainless steel, but the bottom is not). 4) Coupang offers a 2-year warranty. 5) I chose the 2-tier basket type because the 1-tier model takes up too much space due to the large surface area for dishes. (I even measured the size with a tape measure pulled from the sink with the door open). Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Re-installed on Monday ->. I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe length in case I needed to change the door direction, but it was shorter than expected, so the installer kindly adjusted it again and changed the direction.) It's a cycle of going to work, coming home, dinner, washing dishes, doing laundry, doing housework, then sleeping, and then going to work again... Ah. This dishwasher is so convenient. - First day with the dishwasher. I cooked curry rice with meat for dinner tonight. I was worried about the cleaning power, but I wanted to test it out in extreme conditions for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice grains at the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, dishes, cutlery, and the kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature, so it took 80 minutes. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Or like fresh clothes after occasionally washing them at 60 degrees or higher in a washing machine that usually runs at 30 degrees? That kind of feeling. - The slightly burnt-on residue inside the stainless steel pot from cooking didn't come off. Since it was soaked, I scrubbed it in cold water just like hand-washing, and it cleaned up easily. # I removed the 2-tier basket to put large pots and cutting boards in, and I think this is more convenient. # The detergent is marked for 7 grams, but I unknowingly bought 10 grams, so I just used that and there were no problems (7-gram bottles seem to be hard to find). I didn't want to drill a hole, so I removed an unused detergent container from the sink beforehand and asked them to run the pipes through there, and it fits perfectly. As for noise, I don't notice anything other than the sound of the water draining two or three times. For those new to dishwashers, no matter which brand you choose, it will definitely be more convenient than not having one, and I think you will experience a whole new world. I think I'll try working out this evening. Let's just go for it and live comfortably~~~~~

Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Sentence (English): First day with the dishwasher.
Comments (English): I am sharing my purchasing process and my first dishwasher review in case it helps those who, like me, are struggling with their first purchase. First off, I am a dad. Since I lacked the information and experience that moms and housewives might, I spent nearly a month searching for products and reviews. The more I searched, the more confused I became, and the harder it was to make a decision. I set criteria to narrow down my candidates: 1. Mid-range models in case I regretted buying them later. 2. Less than 10% of total reviews must have 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (stainless steel interior). 4. Warranty period. 5. Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. (Interior walls are stainless steel, but the bottom is not). 4) Coupang offers a 2-year warranty. 5) I chose the 2-tier basket type because the 1-tier model takes up too much space due to the large surface area for dishes. (I even measured the size with a tape measure pulled from the sink with the door open). Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Re-installed on Monday ->. I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe length in case I needed to change the door direction, but it was shorter than expected, so the installer kindly adjusted it again and changed the direction.) It's a cycle of going to work, coming home, dinner, washing dishes, doing laundry, doing housework, then sleeping, and then going to work again... Ah. This dishwasher is so convenient. - First day with the dishwasher. I cooked curry rice with meat for dinner tonight. I was worried about the cleaning power, but I wanted to test it out in extreme conditions for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice grains at the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, dishes, cutlery, and the kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature, so it took 80 minutes. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Or like fresh clothes after occasionally washing them at 60 degrees or higher in a washing machine that usually runs at 30 degrees? That kind of feeling. - The slightly burnt-on residue inside the stainless steel pot from cooking didn't come off. Since it was soaked, I scrubbed it in cold water just like hand-washing, and it cleaned up easily. # I removed the 2-tier basket to put large pots and cutting boards in, and I think this is more convenient. # The detergent is marked for 7 grams, but I unknowingly bought 10 grams, so I just used that and there were no problems (7-gram bottles seem to be hard to find). I didn't want to drill a hole, so I removed an unused detergent container from the sink beforehand and asked them to run the pipes through there, and it fits perfectly. As for noise, I don't notice anything other than the sound of the water draining two or three times. For those new to dishwashers, no matter which brand you choose, it will definitely be more convenient than not having one, and I think you will experience a whole new world. I think I'll try working out this evening. Let's just go for it and live comfortably~~~~~

Sentence (English): The time is decreasing).
Comments (English): I am sharing my purchasing process and my first dishwasher review in case it helps those who, like me, are struggling with their first purchase. First off, I am a dad. Since I lacked the information and experience that moms and housewives might, I spent nearly a month searching for products and reviews. The more I searched, the more confused I became, and the harder it was to make a decision. I set criteria to narrow down my candidates: 1. Mid-range models in case I regretted buying them later. 2. Less than 10% of total reviews must have 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (stainless steel interior). 4. Warranty period. 5. Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. (Interior walls are stainless steel, but the bottom is not). 4) Coupang offers a 2-year warranty. 5) I chose the 2-tier basket type because the 1-tier model takes up too much space due to the large surface area for dishes. (I even measured the size with a tape measure pulled from the sink with the door open). Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Re-installed on Monday ->. I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe length in case I needed to change the door direction, but it was shorter than expected, so the installer kindly adjusted it again and changed the direction.) It's a cycle of going to work, coming home, dinner, washing dishes, doing laundry, doing housework, then sleeping, and then going to work again... Ah. This dishwasher is so convenient. - First day with the dishwasher. I cooked curry rice with meat for dinner tonight. I was worried about the cleaning power, but I wanted to test it out in extreme conditions for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice grains at the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, dishes, cutlery, and the kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature, so it took 80 minutes. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Or like fresh clothes after occasionally washing them at 60 degrees or higher in a washing machine that usually runs at 30 degrees? That kind of feeling. - The slightly burnt-on residue inside the stainless steel pot from cooking didn't come off. Since it was soaked, I scrubbed it in cold water just like hand-washing, and it cleaned up easily. # I removed the 2-tier basket to put large pots and cutting boards in, and I think this is more convenient. # The detergent is marked for 7 grams, but I unknowingly bought 10 grams, so I just used that and there were no problems (7-gram bottles seem to be hard to find). I didn't want to drill a hole, so I removed an unused detergent container from the sink beforehand and asked them to run the pipes through there, and it fits perfectly. As for noise, I don't notice anything other than the sound of the water draining two or three times. For those new to dishwashers, no matter which brand you choose, it will definitely be more convenient than not having one, and I think you will experience a whole new world. I think I'll try working out this evening. Let's just go for it and live comfortably~~~~~

Sentence (English): It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while?
Comments (English): I am sharing my purchasing process and my first dishwasher review in case it helps those who, like me, are struggling with their first purchase. First off, I am a dad. Since I lacked the information and experience that moms and housewives might, I spent nearly a month searching for products and reviews. The more I searched, the more confused I became, and the harder it was to make a decision. I set criteria to narrow down my candidates: 1. Mid-range models in case I regretted buying them later. 2. Less than 10% of total reviews must have 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (stainless steel interior). 4. Warranty period. 5. Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. (Interior walls are stainless steel, but the bottom is not). 4) Coupang offers a 2-year warranty. 5) I chose the 2-tier basket type because the 1-tier model takes up too much space due to the large surface area for dishes. (I even measured the size with a tape measure pulled from the sink with the door open). Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Re-installed on Monday ->. I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe length in case I needed to change the door direction, but it was shorter than expected, so the installer kindly adjusted it again and changed the direction.) It's a cycle of going to work, coming home, dinner, washing dishes, doing laundry, doing housework, then sleeping, and then going to work again... Ah. This dishwasher is so convenient. - First day with the dishwasher. I cooked curry rice with meat for dinner tonight. I was worried about the cleaning power, but I wanted to test it out in extreme conditions for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice grains at the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, dishes, cutlery, and the kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature, so it took 80 minutes. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Or like fresh clothes after occasionally washing them at 60 degrees or higher in a washing machine that usually runs at 30 degrees? That kind of feeling. - The slightly burnt-on residue inside the stainless steel pot from cooking didn't come off. Since it was soaked, I scrubbed it in cold water just like hand-washing, and it cleaned up easily. # I removed the 2-tier basket to put large pots and cutting boards in, and I think this is more convenient. # The detergent is marked for 7 grams, but I unknowingly bought 10 grams, so I just used that and there were no problems (7-gram bottles seem to be hard to find). I didn't want to drill a hole, so I removed an unused detergent container from the sink beforehand and asked them to run the pipes through there, and it fits perfectly. As for noise, I don't notice anything other than the sound of the water draining two or three times. For those new to dishwashers, no matter which brand you choose, it will definitely be more convenient than not having one, and I think you will experience a whole new world. I think I'll try working out this evening. Let's just go for it and live comfortably~~~~~

Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Or like fresh clothes after occasionally washing them at 60 degrees or higher in a washing machine that usually runs at 30 degrees? That kind of feeling. - The slightly burnt-on residue inside the stainless steel pot from cooking didn't come off.
