Comments (English): I am sharing my purchasing process and my first dishwasher review in case it helps those who, like me, are struggling with their first purchase. First off, I am a dad. Since I lacked the information and experience that moms and housewives might, I spent nearly a month searching for products and reviews. The more I searched, the more confused I became, and the harder it was to make a decision. I set criteria to narrow down my candidates: 1. Mid-range models in case I regretted buying them later. 2. Less than 10% of total reviews must have 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (stainless steel interior). 4. Warranty period. 5. Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. (Interior walls are stainless steel, but the bottom is not). 4) Coupang offers a 2-year warranty. 5) I chose the 2-tier basket type because the 1-tier model takes up too much space due to the large surface area for dishes. (I even measured the size with a tape measure pulled from the sink with the door open). Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Re-installed on Monday ->. I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe length in case I needed to change the door direction, but it was shorter than expected, so the installer kindly adjusted it again and changed the direction.) It's a cycle of going to work, coming home, dinner, washing dishes, doing laundry, doing housework, then sleeping, and then going to work again... Ah. This dishwasher is so convenient. - First day with the dishwasher. I cooked curry rice with meat for dinner tonight. I was worried about the cleaning power, but I wanted to test it out in extreme conditions for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice grains at the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, dishes, cutlery, and the kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature, so it took 80 minutes. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Or like fresh clothes after occasionally washing them at 60 degrees or higher in a washing machine that usually runs at 30 degrees? That kind of feeling. - The slightly burnt-on residue inside the stainless steel pot from cooking didn't come off. Since it was soaked, I scrubbed it in cold water just like hand-washing, and it cleaned up easily. # I removed the 2-tier basket to put large pots and cutting boards in, and I think this is more convenient. # The detergent is marked for 7 grams, but I unknowingly bought 10 grams, so I just used that and there were no problems (7-gram bottles seem to be hard to find). I didn't want to drill a hole, so I removed an unused detergent container from the sink beforehand and asked them to run the pipes through there, and it fits perfectly. As for noise, I don't notice anything other than the sound of the water draining two or three times. For those new to dishwashers, no matter which brand you choose, it will definitely be more convenient than not having one, and I think you will experience a whole new world. I think I'll try working out this evening. Let's just go for it and live comfortably~~~~~

The more I searched, the more confused I became, and the harder it was to make a decision. I set criteria to narrow down my candidates: 1. Mid-range models in case I regretted buying them later. 2. Less than 10% of total reviews must have 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (stainless steel interior). 4. Warranty period. 5. Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. (Interior walls are stainless steel, but the bottom is not). 4) Coupang offers a 2-year warranty. 5) I chose the 2-tier basket type because the 1-tier model takes up too much space due to the large surface area for dishes. (I even measured the size with a tape measure pulled from the sink with the door open). Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Re-installed on Monday ->. I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe length in case I needed to change the door direction, but it was shorter than expected, so the installer kindly adjusted it again and changed the direction.) It's a cycle of going to work, coming home, dinner, washing dishes, doing laundry, doing housework, then sleeping, and then going to work again... Ah. This dishwasher is so convenient. - First day with the dishwasher. I cooked curry rice with meat for dinner tonight. I was worried about the cleaning power, but I wanted to test it out in extreme conditions for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice grains at the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, dishes, cutlery, and the kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature, so it took 80 minutes. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Or like fresh clothes after occasionally washing them at 60 degrees or higher in a washing machine that usually runs at 30 degrees? That kind of feeling. - The slightly burnt-on residue inside the stainless steel pot from cooking didn't come off. Since it was soaked, I scrubbed it in cold water just like hand-washing, and it cleaned up easily. # I removed the 2-tier basket to put large pots and cutting boards in, and I think this is more convenient. # The detergent is marked for 7 grams, but I unknowingly bought 10 grams, so I just used that and there were no problems (7-gram bottles seem to be hard to find). I didn't want to drill a hole, so I removed an unused detergent container from the sink beforehand and asked them to run the pipes through there, and it fits perfectly. As for noise, I don't notice anything other than the sound of the water draining two or three times. For those new to dishwashers, no matter which brand you choose, it will definitely be more convenient than not having one, and I think you will experience a whole new world. I think I'll try working out this evening. Let's just go for it and live comfortably~~~~~

Sentence (English): I think I'll try working out this evening.
Comments (English): I am sharing my purchasing process and my first dishwasher review in case it helps those who, like me, are struggling with their first purchase. First off, I am a dad. Since I lacked the information and experience that moms and housewives might, I spent nearly a month searching for products and reviews. The more I searched, the more confused I became, and the harder it was to make a decision. I set criteria to narrow down my candidates: 1. Mid-range models in case I regretted buying them later. 2. Less than 10% of total reviews must have 1 to 3 stars. 3. Cleaning power + durability (stainless steel interior). 4. Warranty period. 5. Size that doesn't take up too much space on the sink counter. 1) The 200,000 to 300,000 won range seemed to be a proven choice. 2-3) I analyzed that people with experience using dishwashers are capable of clearly distinguishing the pros and cons of a new product compared to what they have used, so they generally tend to have lower star ratings. (Interior walls are stainless steel, but the bottom is not). 4) Coupang offers a 2-year warranty. 5) I chose the 2-tier basket type because the 1-tier model takes up too much space due to the large surface area for dishes. (I even measured the size with a tape measure pulled from the sink with the door open). Purchased on Saturday -> Installed on Sunday -> Re-installed on Monday ->. I do the evening dishes in the dishwasher. (I requested a longer pipe length in case I needed to change the door direction, but it was shorter than expected, so the installer kindly adjusted it again and changed the direction.) It's a cycle of going to work, coming home, dinner, washing dishes, doing laundry, doing housework, then sleeping, and then going to work again... Ah. This dishwasher is so convenient. - First day with the dishwasher. I cooked curry rice with meat for dinner tonight. I was worried about the cleaning power, but I wanted to test it out in extreme conditions for the first time. - I roughly removed the rice grains at the sink faucet and put in the greasy pot, cutting board, dishes, cutlery, and the kids' water bottles. - I set it to high temperature, so it took 80 minutes. (The time is decreasing). The washing finished at 12 minutes, but it started cooling down from that point. At 3 minutes, the door opened and steam shot up. Out of curiosity, I placed my hand on the back of the top panel, and the back was scorching hot. - After about 5 more minutes, I took them out, and the condition was noticeably different. It felt like the before and after of scrubbing the kids for the first time in a while? Or like fresh clothes after occasionally washing them at 60 degrees or higher in a washing machine that usually runs at 30 degrees? That kind of feeling. - The slightly burnt-on residue inside the stainless steel pot from cooking didn't come off. Since it was soaked, I scrubbed it in cold water just like hand-washing, and it cleaned up easily. # I removed the 2-tier basket to put large pots and cutting boards in, and I think this is more convenient. # The detergent is marked for 7 grams, but I unknowingly bought 10 grams, so I just used that and there were no problems (7-gram bottles seem to be hard to find). I didn't want to drill a hole, so I removed an unused detergent container from the sink beforehand and asked them to run the pipes through there, and it fits perfectly. As for noise, I don't notice anything other than the sound of the water draining two or three times. For those new to dishwashers, no matter which brand you choose, it will definitely be more convenient than not having one, and I think you will experience a whole new world. I think I'll try working out this evening. Let's just go for it and live comfortably~~~~~

Sentence (English): This dishwasher cleans and dries extremely well.
Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher…poor racks ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher cleans and dries extremely well. And it's super quiet. So quiet they include a red light shining on the floor so you know it's still running. Dishes are super clean and dry when they come out of the washer. And the shallow upper rack (3rd rack) is extremely helpful to wash small items and sharp knives. So what's the problem? The main racks don't stack very well. The lower rack tines are too closely spaced so it's one dinner plate every other spot. The bottle Washer attachment just gets in the way and the wine glass holders just get in the way with regular glasses. Not to mention the edge of the upper main rack is too narrow to support mid to large glasses. Just an overall crummy rack design. If you have a large family then you may find the capacity to small due to loading issues. So 4*s instead of a 5* review.

But if you go to the hardware store (I went to several), nobody will know what you're talking about or what it is.  That's because everyone else in the country calls that thing a '3/8 inch cable clamp for 1/2 inch knock-out'.  Took me half a day of running around before I stumbled on that important fact.Another installation thing (that turned out not to be much of an issue for me, but might for you) is that the levelers for the rear of the dishwasher can't be adjusted after it is pushed under the counter.  My old dishwasher had screws on the front that adjusted the rear levelers.

Sentence (English): I was worried about replacing our 15 setting Westinghouse of 7 yrs with this new 14 place dishwasher but after a couple of months, I am so happy with the purchase.
Comments (English): [ Whisper Quiet and Great Cleaning Ability ] || ---------------- || I was worried about replacing our 15 setting Westinghouse of 7 yrs with this new 14 place dishwasher but after a couple of months, I am so happy with the purchase. I do have a Bosch washing machine so new it was a reliable and reputable brand. It has heaps of room and adjustable shelves - you can even fit baking trays in it which my other dishwasher couldn't. The biggest positive - it is whisper quiet - don't even know it is on half the time and cleans super well. I had heard because of the plastic base, it would be noisier but this is not the case at all. The "new plastic smell" some customers have complained about was gone after a couple of washes. I have just been using the same ECO Wash setting every time and every wash is perfect. My only minor negative is some of the items don't dry & stay wet at the end of the wash but enough positives that I can overlook this. Also don't leave the RINSE AID door open - you can't close the dishwasher and it could damage it or break off if you used force. Great purchase for the price

Have had this dishwasher for about 2 months now and it cleans like a dream. It's virtually silent, especially compared to the GE (sounded like an airplane taking off). I read the manual and followed the directions regarding just scrapping your dishes and loading them and it's a game changer. And to be able to load dishes at any level (even plastic) has made doing dishes easier. I've even ran cake pans, dried on casseroles dishes, and spaghetti stained pans and they come out clean without any scrubbing or rinsing. I just can't believe that a dishwasher works this great with little effort. The app that goes with the dishwasher is great too! It will tell you when to run a clean cycle, when to clean the filter, and if you set it up, it will tell you when you're almost out of dishwasher tabs. It will alert you when the cycle is complete and when updates are needed and complete. Finally, the exterior is beautiful and easy to keep clean. I really can't say enough about how great this dishwasher is. LOVE IT!

Sentence (English): I trusted Coupang and LG brands and purchased the dishwasher above, but a defective product was delivered.
Comments (English): [ I received a defective washing machine and it is so hard to return it. ] || ---------------- || I trusted Coupang and LG brands and purchased the dishwasher above, but a defective product was delivered. I requested a refund after returning it, but LG did not process it smoothly, causing me great inconvenience in my life. The \"lower dish rack\" of the delivered dishwasher is stuck in the dishwasher drum and does not move, so I cannot put dishes in the dishwasher. Sentence (English): I had to replace my previous dishwasher from 2006 (thanks to a power surge after my neighborhood lost power), and I had limited choices in a biscuit color.
Comments (English): I had to replace my previous dishwasher from 2006 (thanks to a power surge after my neighborhood lost power), and I had limited choices in a biscuit color. This was the only one I could find with the feature of delaying the start of the wash cycle like my old one had. (This one can be set for any number of hours from 1-24). I have to say I was pleasantly surprised at how quiet the dishwasher is. It is also more spacious on the inside than my old one, so the largest plates do not touch each other when placed next to each other front to back or hit the cleaning arm as I am pulling the bottom tray in and out. However, I cannot fit as many bowls and glasses in the middle tray or as many plates in the bottom tray because of the placement of the tines in the trays, which I am not liking as much as my previous one. I used to be able to have a row of glasses between each row of bowls and the side of the tray, but there is not enough space for that in this model. It's basically wasted space. I also used to be able to put three small plates in a row front to back instead of 2 larger plates but cannot do that with this model. Plus, when I push the trays back in, the dishes are not held in place very well and tend to move, even though I am trying to push them very gently. This is also because of the design of the trays and placement of the tines. I have to put some of the dishes back where they should be the next time I pull the tray out before loading more dishes in it. That's not helpful. Plus, I'm worried my glasses in the middle tray will hit each other and break when they don't stay upright. I don't think I will use the top tray for spatulas and other small items much, but I'm sure those who would use it will like it. The adjustable height of the middle rack is handy, but even with it on the higher setting, I am having to reach down farther to pull it out because of the added top tray. The door is VERY tight so far, so I really have to push it down when opening it so I can pull out the bottom tray, which is annoying. Hopefully, it will loosen up over time. I do not like that the controls are on the top edge of the door either. That means I have to bend down to look below the counter to see how much time is left etc., or I have to open the door if I want to stop the cycle or change a setting because you can't push any buttons when the door is closed. I'd rather have the controls on the front, which is more practical. I wish it did not have the stainless steel strip along the front, as all of my other appliances are just plain biscuit color, but perhaps when I have to replace them, it will blend in more as they will likely have to be stainless steel. Overall, there are more things that I dislike about this model compared to my old one vs. things that I like better, so I am only giving it 3 stars. If I could have kept my old one, I would rather still have that one as it was more user friendly and practical.
